README: COMMITTED BASELINE for scripts/lint-no-domain-in-builtin.mjs — the 2026-07-28 full-tree
domain audit (.lifecycle/processor-ui-language/DOMAIN_AUDIT.md) found 25 HIGH domain leaks
that every existing guard was scoped too narrowly to see. The guard was widened to see them,
which makes it RED against the tree as it stands today. Narrowing it back is the exact failure
that round exists to stop, so today's violations are recorded here instead.
RATCHET: observed > count fails (a NEW leak). observed < count fails as STALE — shrink it in
the same commit with `node scripts/lint-no-domain-in-builtin.mjs --prune-baseline`, which only
ever LOWERS or REMOVES entries and never adds one. A new entry must be argued for by hand.
HOUSE STYLE THAT FOLLOWS FROM THAT, for test code: a SHARED HELPER MAY NOT CONTAIN A DOMAIN
TOKEN. The ratchet is shrink-only PER FILE, so a file with no entry has a budget of ZERO —
the first token in a NEW helper is a new leak and the gate goes red, and `--prune-baseline`
cannot rescue it (it never adds an entry). Pane- and DOM-addressing code therefore stays in
the SPECS, which already carry that residue and whose counts do not move; the helper takes
the attribute name / selector / test-id prefix as a PARAMETER and stays generic. Worked
example: `ui/tests/viz-e2e/_helpers.ts` holds zero `viz-cell` occurrences (`cell` is a
token) while the specs that pass them in hold all of them. Exempting test directories was
considered and REFUSED: those trees were invisible to this guard until WS-R4 and the
invisibility was the finding, and an exemption lands on exactly the code most likely to
spread a spelling — one token in a helper is a token in every spec that imports it. Fuller
statement, with the cost: the README's "Writing a shared test helper" section, and the
block beside the RATCHET semantics in lint-no-domain-in-builtin.mjs.
`finding` is the DOMAIN_AUDIT id (E1-E6 frontend extensions, C1-C8 frontend core, S1-S11
server, B1-B3 the three real bugs) so this file reads as a WORKLIST. Non-finding tags:
DEC-J           a retained view_spec LANGUAGE key (`obs`) — a rename here is a versioned
language change, not a hygiene sweep
DEC-M           a retained WIRE CONTRACT field (cell_count/gene_count)
FALSE-POSITIVE  confirmed non-domain use (DOMAIN_AUDIT §7) — e.g. dock GRID `cells`
GENERIC         an ambiguous token used in its generic software sense (a metric `sample`)
DOC-EXAMPLE     (WS-C) a domain ILLUSTRATION in a doc comment on a domain-agnostic mechanism
("e.g. `single-cell/anndata`", "a `(comparison,gene)` DE table"). Deliberately
retained: deleting the example to satisfy a scanner is the failure mode the
domain-prose severity exists to avoid.
DOC-CHANGELOG   (WS-C) prose that RECORDS a domain leak having been REMOVED (the C8 seam note,
S8's "this doc used to justify itself with one domain tool's build matrix",
"the DE-specific heuristic is GONE"). Deleting it loses the reason.
W1-W12          (WS-C) NEW findings surfaced by the widened scan set — see DOMAIN_AUDIT §9.
RESIDUE         RETIRED. It meant "real domain vocabulary, not individually triaged": 9 entries
/ 37 hits / 6 files, the only pocket with no owner and no decision. WS-C triaged
all nine, and the guard now REJECTS the tag so the bucket cannot refill.
`code` is keyed <path relative to src-app> -> <token> -> {count, finding, note}.
`prose` (comment text only, a lower severity) is keyed <path> -> either a bare TOTAL COUNT
(the 2026-07-28 WS-B bulk record) or {count, finding, note}. The object form is REQUIRED for
every prose entry added or RAISED since — a raised budget must say why it rose.
2026-07-28 RECONCILIATION (post five-workstream merge). `--prune-baseline` removed 61 stale
code entries (152 -> 91) as the open-axis migration + the two domain strips landed; the 94
remaining findings were then triaged one by one: 11 REWORDED (gratuitous domain illustrations
in doc comments — `single-cell/anndata`, `h5ad_import.py`, `AnnDataInspector.tsx`, `Cell
Ranger`, `"Cluster {embedding}"`, `per-cell column data`, … all replaced with neutral examples),
83 BASELINED here with a reason, 0 new real leaks. Prose that EXPLAINS a domain-agnostic fix
(jobsCapability's `the workbench inventing a single-cell file format on a format-neutral
backend`, the C8 seam changelogs, the S4 quoted script) is baselined DELIBERATELY: deleting the
explanation to satisfy a scanner is the failure mode the domain-prose severity exists to avoid.
2026-07-28 WS-C — THE SCAN SET IS NOW THE TREE. Pre-WS-C the guard saw `server/src/modules/**`
+ `ui/src/modules/workbench/**` + TWO named files: 353 files, i.e. less than half the codebase.
It now scans SEVEN roots (633 files), each with its own committed file-count floor:
rust 161 / rustRoot 5 / buildHelper 3 / desktop 6 / workbenchFe 190 / uiFe 260 / packagesFe 8.
`packages/viz` is a DOCUMENTED CARVE-OUT by construction (owner decision) — the guard hand-lists
the packages it scans, so viz is simply never built into the set; the measured cost (62 domain
tokens in the library core, 144 in showcase/stories, and nothing preventing new ones) is stated
in the guard next to the list. Any OTHER package that is neither scanned nor documented FAILS.
WS-C also closed the VOCABULARY gap: +10 nouns (`enrichment`, `pct_mito`, `transcriptome`,
`vis2D`, `scanpy`, `seurat`, `mtx`, `h5mu`, `tiledbsoma`, `GRCh38`) and a new CASE-SENSITIVE
acronym tier (`DE`, `QC`, `BAM`) with a non-alphanumeric boundary — the ordinary boundary gives
`DE` 1575 hits (`DERIVED`/`DESIGN`/`DEC-5`) and the strict one gives 41, all genuine. `vis2D` is
the literal DOMAIN_AUDIT E6 is about and was invisible; `tiledbsoma` was invisible because the
camel boundary refuses `tiledb`+`soma`. Fallout: 596 code / 1399 prose hits (was 549 / 1085),
and the ledger grew 92 -> 108 code entries in 77 files and 143 -> 183 prose files. NOTHING was
narrowed to stay green.
NEW `literals` TIER (WS-C). `substring` / `quoted-id` / `quoted-title` — a hardcoded domain
datatype-id LITERAL, the hardest INV-3 kind — had no baseline at all, i.e. zero tolerance, which
was only survivable while half the tree was unscanned. The widening surfaced THREE real ones
(`main.rs`'s `--help` blurb; `build_helper`'s `env-rootfs/single-cell/` path, twice). They are
RECORDED under a CEILING, not a ratchet with room: the hit count may only go DOWN, and raising
`LITERAL_HITS_CEILING` is an explicit, reviewable admission.
WS-C MERGE NOTE (read before merging the sibling `ui/src` domain-strip workstream). This
baseline was measured on THIS worktree. The sibling branch FIXED leaks in `ui/src/**` that are
still present here (e.g. `UploadPanel.tsx["h5ad"] = 2` goes to 0), so on merge this file will be
STALE in exactly those files — which is the ratchet working, not a break. Run
`node scripts/lint-no-domain-in-builtin.mjs --prune-baseline` IN THE MERGE COMMIT; it only ever
lowers or removes, never adds. Entries the sibling cited as false positives are already tagged
and noted here (arrowClient `cells` = table cells; visualization/adapter `Cell`/`CELL` = grid
cells; TimeSeriesChart `samples` = CPU/mem samples; ProvenanceSettingsCard `feature` = software
feature; api-client/types.ts = GENERATED, W7).
WS-C KNOWN GAP, stated rather than hidden: the JS guard is now STRICTLY WIDER than its Rust twin
(`server/tests/domain_surface/mod.rs`), which still walks only `server/src/modules/**` with the
pre-WS-C 24-token vocabulary and no acronym tier. Both halves still read THIS file, and WS-C
removed no `code` entry and changed no `code` count, so the twin cannot have been broken by it —
but porting the 10 new nouns + the DE/QC/BAM acronym boundary to the Rust side is outstanding.
2026-07-28 ROUND-1 MERGE RECONCILIATION (the WS-C MERGE NOTE above, executed). `ds-uix` and
`ds-guard2` merged into `feat/processor-ui-language`; `--prune-baseline` then removed 8 entries
and lowered 1, all in the files the merge note predicted: UploadPanel `h5ad` 2 -> 0 and `mtx`
17 -> 0, dataSource `gene` 1 -> 0, ProjectAdminPage `cells`/`genes`/`cell`/`gene` 1 -> 0 each,
prose dataSource 6 -> 5 and workstore/catalog 2 -> 0. Nothing was raised or added by the tool.
Two NEW prose hits fell outside the ledger, both DOC-CHANGELOG and both authored BY the strip
as provenance for what it removed: UploadPanel:128 "(Was `mtxMode` — named after ONE format.)"
(prose raised 7 -> 8 with the reason on the entry) and the new ProjectFormDrawer entry, which
records that the project-name placeholder used to read "e.g. PBMC atlas 2026". Both are kept
verbatim for the standing reason: deleting an explanation to satisfy the scanner is the exact
failure the domain-prose severity exists to prevent. The ProjectFormDrawer one earns its keep
twice over — the copy it describes contained NO vocabulary token, so it documents a class of
leak (the PURPOSE of a sentence, not its nouns) that this scanner structurally cannot detect.
══ WS-R3 (2026-07-28) — FOUR HOLES CLOSED; THIS FILE GREW BY DESIGN ══
An adversarial audit found the previous green was partly an artifact of what the guard
REFUSED to look at. Closing that took the scan set 633 -> 702 files and the ledger
67 -> 197 code entries / 168 -> 192 prose files / 0 -> 69 LITERAL hits. Nothing below was
added to the tree by this round; all of it was already there and structurally invisible.
New `finding` tags, one per hole, so every added entry names WHY it is newly visible:
R3-DEBUG    the guard BLANKED `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` item blocks, which made almost
all of `workstore/data_api.rs` invisible (baselined 104 prose / 0 code for a
file measuring ~398 raw hits) even though it registers SIX real HTTP routes.
245 code + 88 prose + 23 LITERAL. `#[cfg(test)]` stays blanked — see the
`stripCfgBlocks` doc comment for that decision and its measured cost.
R3-EXT      both guards read only .rs/.ts/.tsx (633 of 1108 app+test code files). The
app EMBEDS four more formats: .sql migrations, two `include_str!`-ed and
EXECUTED `seed_*.py` drivers, baked .json manifests, and it SHIPS
`ui/openapi/openapi.json`. 264 code + 12 literal in openapi.json alone.
R3-GALLERY  the `gallery.tsx` / `cassette.ts` BASENAME exemption (10 files, 190 hits) was
claimable by naming a file — the same property this guard's own WS-B header
condemns in the `/gallery/` DIRECTORY exemption it removed. Now scanned.
R3-TOKEN    five tokens absent from the vocabulary for no reason but omission, in files
the guard ALREADY read: PBMC, nCount, pct_ribo (whose sibling pct_mito WAS
listed), ident, 10x. 26 hits.
`prose` IS NOW PER (file, TOKEN), like `code`. It used to be a per-file TOTAL decremented
without inspecting the token, so 1268 hits across 168 files were FUNGIBLE: any file with an
entry could absorb a brand-new leak of a DIFFERENT token for free. `ui/src/api-client/
types.ts` (75) is the case that matters most — it is GENERATED, regenerated wholesale, so a
new domain doc-comment on a backend type landed there and was absorbed silently.
Shape: <path> -> { finding?, note?, tokens: { <token>: <count> } }. The old per-file-total
spellings are REJECTED, not grandfathered: leaving a fungible spelling readable would leave
the hole open.
WS-R4 (2026-07-28) — THE TEST TREES. `testCode` / `testProse` / `testLiterals`.
`server/tests/**` and `ui/tests/**` were in NO scan root at all. That is a stronger
statement than "#[cfg(test)] blanking hid them": the blanking never applied, because the
walk never reached the directories. Nobody had ever looked. Round 3's own header said so
(finding R3-F1) and deferred it; this is that round.
FOUR HOLES CLOSED, and every entry below names which one surfaced it:
R4-TESTS-RS       server/tests/**.rs — the backend integration suite (118 files).
R4-TESTS-FIXTURE  server/tests/** .py/.yaml the suite reads or executes (14 files).
R4-TESTS-E2E      ui/tests/** — the Playwright suite (184 files).
R4-TESTS-UNIT     *.test.* / *.spec.* under ui/src + the scanned packages (128 files).
These were INSIDE a scanned root DIRECTORY the whole time and were
dropped by BASENAME alone — the exemption round 3 flagged as having
the same claimable-by-naming weakness as the gallery.tsx one it had
just removed, and could not close without opening the test trees.
R4-TESTS-SUPPORT  __fixtures__/ + __testutil__/ (3 files) — the DIRECTORY form of the
same weakness, retired on the same grounds.
R4-TESTS-CARD     the 8 test files carrying an EXACT-CARDINALITY certification. Given
their own id because they are qualitatively different from an
incidental domain example: they make the APP suite FAIL if the
contributed bundle is deleted or changes size. See
CARDINALITY_CERTIFICATIONS in lint-no-domain-in-builtin.mjs for the
pinned anchors and the full 14-entry ledger.
THE BASENAME QUESTION, resolved. `#[cfg(test)]` stays blanked — it is COMPILER-ENFORCED,
so it cannot be claimed without the code genuinely not shipping, and its cost is measured
and on the record. A BASENAME has no such enforcement: the same property that makes
`*.spec.ts` a reliable collector for vitest/playwright makes it a reliable DODGE. So the
basename is kept as a CLASSIFIER (it decides which TIER a finding lands in) and retired as
an EXEMPTION (it no longer decides whether the file is READ). Every by-name exemption in
the guard is now gone; the survivors are the two named workbench gallery-seed DATA files
and the compiler-enforced Rust ones.
WHY A SEPARATE NAMESPACE. Merging ~6100 test hits into code/prose/literals is one line of
code and destroys the three numbers that carry a hard meaning: the production literal
ceiling (69 — "this many hardcoded domain datatype ids SHIP"), the production noun floor
(a COLLAPSE detector that a four-figure test total would mask completely), and the
production entry count (the readable worklist). The test tier therefore has its own three
sections, its own floors (TEST_OBSERVATION_FLOORS), its own ceiling
(TEST_LITERAL_HITS_CEILING) and its own report line. A production regression stays visible
at production scale.
SELF-REFERENCE, stated. `server/tests/domain_surface/mod.rs` — the Rust twin of the guard
— is now IN the scan set, and it must spell the forbidden vocabulary out in order to
search for it. Its residue is baselined like any other file. The consequence is deliberate
and good: ADDING a vocabulary token to the twin now raises its own baseline entry, which
requires an explicit edit here. A future round widening the vocabulary should expect that,
not treat it as a bug.
NOT SCANNED, by decision (each with its reason, so the omission is on the record):
processors/**, incl. processors/*/tests/** (~16 pytest files) — the CONTRIBUTED DOMAIN
ITSELF, as DATA. processors/single-cell-types/manifest.yaml IS the lattice the app
must not contain, and a processor's own pytest suite is that package testing its own
domain, which is what a contributed package is FOR. Scanning it would be a category
error — the same one round 3 recorded for the production side.
packages/viz/tests/** (20 .mjs) — follows the pre-existing owner carve-out on
packages/viz. Measured: none of them reference a domain datatype id.
server/src/modules/**/tests/** — TEST-ONLY BY DECLARATION, the compiler-enforced
exclusion. Unchanged. It costs four of the fourteen cardinality certifications, which
is why those are pinned by an ANCHOR ledger rather than by the scan.
*.sh (2 files) — no .sh dialect exists in either tokenizer; adding one is a new-dialect
decision, not a root decision. *.gz / *.h5ad — binary.
RANKED WORKLIST for a later round (these are RECORDED here, not fixed — WS-R4 owns the
guard and the ledger, not the test suites):
1. ui/tests/e2e/datatype/sniff.spec.ts:30 — asserts a .csv sniffs to the `de` datatype
while the Rust twin (datatype/sniff.rs) now asserts .csv -> None, because the
producer-less `de` type was PRUNED. An already-DIVERGENT hard membership claim on a
datatype that no longer ships, sitting green in a tree no guard had ever read. This
is the single clearest payoff for looking, and it is a correctness bug, not debt.
2. R4-CARD-01 / R4-CARD-09 — the shared 26-entry lattice_golden.json, asserted
exact-count in Rust and exact-parity in the browser. The Rust file's own comment
still itemises it as "22 (6 roots + 15 single-cell + annotation-table)": the
itemisation is ALREADY STALE while the assertion passes. One fixture, two suites, so
a fix has to move both.
3. R4-CARD-02 — BAKED_20 pins the domain processors' view-action set at exactly 20. It
is a behaviour-preservation proof for a migration that has landed, so it is the most
likely of the fourteen to be retirable outright rather than rewritten.
4. R4-CARD-05 — datatype_contribution_test.rs's hardcoded 15-row parity table: the
single largest verbatim copy of the contributed lattice inside the app suite.
5. R4-CARD-11..14 — the four *.test.ts exact-set assertions against shipped processor
manifests (qcSurface, cellFilterSurface, launcherAvailability). Cheapest to fix:
derive the expectation from the manifest the test already loads.
6. R4-CARD-03/04/06/07/08 — the remaining exact-cardinality assertions.
7. ~16 SOFT membership certifications (assert a domain id is PRESENT but tolerate
additions) are NOT pinned in the ledger — pinning them would make it a second
baseline. They live in the testCode/testLiterals entries and should be swept after
the HARD ones. Largest clusters: server/tests/extensions/*, ui/tests/e2e/workbench/
workbench-registry.spec.ts, ui/tests/e2e/datatype/registry.spec.ts.
══ 2026-07-28 ROUND-4 RECONCILIATION (post five-workstream merge: r4spec, r4embed, ══
══ r4dataapi, r4squash, r4tests) ══
THE HEADLINE: the PRODUCTION tiers shrank harder than in any previous round, and every
unit of the drop is attributed to a named workstream by the `--prune-baseline` diff in
the same commit (an UNACCOUNTED drop is the exact signature the floors exist to catch).
code    1118 -> 726 (-392): r4dataapi 257 (`workstore/data_api.rs` 261 -> 6 + `routes.rs`
2 -> 0), r4spec 94 (`ui/openapi/openapi.json` 107 -> 13), r4squash 37 (the five
module-local migrations that carried domain column comments)
prose   1443 -> 1035 (-408): r4dataapi 180, r4spec 148 (`api-client/types.ts` 74 -> 11,
`datatype/types.rs` 58 -> 5, `extensions/types.rs` 18 -> 1, + 6 module files),
r4squash 78, r4embed 1 (`sandbox/env_image.rs`)
literals  69 -> 34 (-35): r4dataapi 23, r4spec 12. The SHIPPED API contract and the
debug-seed surface both went to ZERO, including the three executable-dispatch
lines WS-R3 had called out by number.
`--prune-baseline` removed 168 entries and lowered 38 (2398 -> 2230 flattened entries,
8772 -> 7915 hits); an independent flatten-and-compare confirmed 0 grew and 0 were added.
THE ONE THING THE TOOL COULD NOT DO — 55 HAND-ARGUED ENTRIES, TWO TAGS:
R4-RELOCATED (45 new + 10 raised, in `_fixtures.ts` + `_seed.ts` under
`ui/tests/e2e/14-declarative-qc/`). r4dataapi replaced six subject-specific
`_debug/seed-*` routes with ONE generic engine and RELOCATED their fixture vocabulary
out of the server crate into the e2e module where the callers already live. Same
bytes, moved from a tier that SHIPS to a tier that only RUNS. A SEVENTH test-tier tag
rather than a reuse of `R4-TESTS-E2E`, whose meaning is 'was here all along and no
guard could see it' — the largest production->test transfer of the whole effort would
have been unreadable folded into that. It is why `TEST_LITERAL_HITS_CEILING` RISES
543 -> 548 while `LITERAL_HITS_CEILING` falls 69 -> 34: 612 -> 582 across both, and
the 35 that left are the ones the binary used to carry.
R3-META (2 raised, `server/tests/domain_surface/mod.rs` prose `cell` 40 -> 45 and
`embedding` 2 -> 3). The round-3 class, unchanged: a FIXING commit's own comment
naming the token it deleted. Here it is this reconciliation's doc comments recording
what r4dataapi removed. Deleting the explanation to satisfy the scanner is the exact
failure the domain-prose severity exists to prevent.
THE WITNESS COLLISION r4squash + r4tests created, and how it was resolved. Both rounds
edited `MUST_SCAN_KEYS` and the `serverData` floor independently and git merged both
without a conflict, so the merged result asserted something false: r4tests had re-anchored
the `.sql` witness on `202608020001_workstore_open_axes.sql` arguing 'migrations are
append-only and are never deleted', and r4squash then DELETED it (49 module-local
migrations -> 8 baselines). The guard went red and named the file, which is the check
working. Resolution: the `.sql` witness is re-pointed at the surviving baseline (a squash
IS a coverage-relevant event and re-pointing is a one-line reviewable edit), and the
real gap — `.py` had NO durable identity pin, because its only two files are deletable
`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` seed drivers — is closed by a NEW mechanism rather than by a
new brittle name: `FORMAT_COVERAGE_PINS` (JS) /
`the_server_data_root_covers_every_format_it_walks` (Rust) probe the tree for each
extension INDEPENDENTLY of the walk and fail only when files of that format exist but the
walk reached none. Vacuous on deletion, un-dodgeable by an exemption, names no file. Both
halves carry a negative control.
MEASURED STATE (both enforcers agree file-for-file via `DOMAIN_SURFACE_DUMP`):
scan set 1115 files across 14 roots (was 702 pre-WS-R4 / 1150 as r4tests reported on
its own tree). PRODUCTION 726 code / 1035 prose / 34 literals in 147 entries / 66 files.
TEST 4011 code / 1844 prose / 548 literals in 834 entries / 240 files.
Rust-twin server-only slice: prod 48 pairs / 186 hits / 431 prose / 3 literals;
test 373 pairs / 1544 hits / 838 prose / 298 literals.

STRIP-SINGLE-CELL RE-BASE (ITEM-4). The single-cell modules, the dock/viz libs, the processor packages and their test trees left; --prune-baseline removed 2021 stale entries and 17 lowered. The KEPT tree's residue was then absorbed in the same commit: 259 new (file, token) pairs across the kept TxResBench surface, dispositioned per file — FALSE-POSITIVE for the kept measurement-table vocabulary (CSV cells / RFC-4180 codec, feature columns and markers, timing/resample samples, the method catalogue's gene-and-feature metadata, the model registry's feature keys, the results-table grid cells), GENERIC for the truly generic senses (help copy, example rows, embedded-payload wording, software feature flag), DOC-CHANGELOG for the strip-note prose that records what ITEM-2/3 removed (the word single-cell is the record itself), W7 for the generated OpenAPI / Tauri contract mirrors, R4-TESTS-RS / R4-TESTS-UNIT / R4-TESTS-E2E for the test tiers. Every token was classified by looking at the site, not the scanner; genuinely single-cell-specific words in kept code were none. The four BASELINE_ENTRY_CEILINGS and both literal ceilings moved to the new measurements in the same commit, and the scan-set/floors/must-scan/census/cardinality constants were re-anchored with the same argument (SCAN_FLOORS etc. in lint-no-domain-in-builtin.mjs).
